At join the node sends a nonce to the machine itself. The device's secure element signs it with its endorsement key, the node verifies the vendor certificate chain and hashes that key, so one chip backs one seat and the check repeats every epoch. Software emulators sign happily and carry no vendor cert.

Fifty seats need fifty real boards. A used mini PC with a TPM runs 150 dollars, so 7,500 dollars up front, plus 250 dollars monthly for power and hosting.

A cedar post rots where tide meets air, basalt holds the wharf, and an inlet silts up whether or not anyone watches.
